subject: MAP & pilot economics — CloudArc pilot (evaluation -> commit milestones)
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@cloudarc.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-02T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & pilot economics — CloudArc pilot (evaluation -> commit milestones)

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for taking the demo last week. Per our conversation, I've attached a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) and a draft SOW that tie the pilot evaluation milestones to commercial outcomes. Key proposal highlights: 

- 30-day evaluation (start-of-pilot -> demo handoff) with 1M inference tokens included as evaluation credit.
- Post-eval ramp: monthly commit schedule for first 3 months (3M / 6M / 12M) with discounts tied to meeting MAP milestones (on-time deployment, latency targets, integration checklist).
- Pricing protection: proposed 12-month protection from go-live for committed tiers; pricing redlines we expect from legal are called out in the attached SOW.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups with retroactive adjustments limited to the committed tier and a 5% reconciliation cap.

Can you review the attached MAP (CloudArc_MAP_v1.xlsx) and let me know if the milestone definitions match what your engineering and procurement teams need? If procurement/legal want different language around "billable usage" (we define this as inference tokens processed by the runtime, excluding cached prefixes and internal health calls), please flag the exact wording you prefer so we can propose redlines.

Next steps I suggest: procurement and legal review this week, tech validation by your engineers (we can host a focused session), then finalize commercial terms by May 14 to keep the projected mid-June go-live.

Attachments: CloudArc_MAP_v1.xlsx, Redwood_SOW_draft_v3.docx

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara@cloudarc.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudarc.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & pilot economics — CloudArc pilot (evaluation -> commit milestones)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the MAP and SOW — quick initial read and procurement/legal flagged a few items we'd like clarified before we can sign off: 

1) True-ups: we need clarity on whether the true-up applies only to overages vs committed tiers or whether retroactive price changes can be applied to prior invoices. Our preference is reconciliations only (no retroactive rate changes).
2) Price protection: 12 months is reasonable, but legal requests a carve-out if material changes in third-party GPU costs occur.
3) Definition of "billable usage": procurement is concerned about server-side caching or intermediate proxies inflating counts. We need explicit exclusions and a sampling method for audits.
4) Ramp credits/discounts: Billing wants to see formula tying completion of MAP milestones to discount amounts (e.g., 10% at milestone 2).

Also attaching our procurement intake form — can you confirm whether Redwood will accept the standard PO flow or requires DocuSign?

Attachment: Procurement_Security_Form.pdf

Appreciate a consolidated response we can circulate internally.

Best,
Sara Patel
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudArc Solutions

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@cloudarc.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & pilot economics — CloudArc pilot (evaluation -> commit milestones)

Sara — thanks, all great points. Consolidated responses below so procurement/legal have text to circulate (I also attached a clean SOW redline in this thread):

1) True-ups: Redwood proposes quarterly reconciliation where true-ups apply to consumption above the committed tier. We will not retroactively increase unit prices on already-invoiced usage; adjustments are limited to billing for uncovered usage quantities. We will include a 30-day dispute window post-invoice.

2) Price protection: we can accept a 12-month price protection window from go-live. We will add a limited force-majeure/third-party-costs clause allowing both parties to renegotiate if GPU spot market prices rise by >40% for a sustained 30-day period. This is a narrow carve-out and subject to mutual agreement.

3) Definition of billable usage: proposed language — "Billable usage = inference tokens consumed by customer requests processed by Redwood runtime, excluding cached prefix tokens served from customer-controlled persistent KV caches, health checks, and internal system diagnostic calls. Third-party proxy traffic will be excluded where the request_id header indicates relay traffic." We will accept sampling-based audits (quarterly) and provide raw usage logs via our console export for a 90-day window.

4) Ramp discounts & MAP tie: suggested formula in SOW: 5% discount when milestone 1 (integration + latency SLOs) completes, additional 5% at milestone 3 (30-day ramp to committed throughput). Discounts apply to committed tier billables only and do not stack beyond a 10% total.

Procurement flow: we accept standard PO workflows and DocuSign. For enterprise deals we usually run signature via DocuSign; PO is OK if sent to billing@redwood.ai and referencing DL-2026-0032.

I've asked legal (cc'ed: neha_kapoor) to prepare redlines for the force-majeure pricing clause and the audit language. Rafael — can you confirm we can honor the 10% max discount cap and the 1M eval credit in the pricing model?

Best,
Lauren

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-06T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MAP & pilot economics — CloudArc pilot (evaluation -> commit milestones)

Folks — forwarding CloudArc's notes and my draft responses. Quick internal asks before I send final redline: 

- Approve capped discount structure (max 10% tied to MAP completion) and confirm we can model the 1M token eval credit as a billable credit (no cash-back). Rafael, please confirm pricing ledger entries and whether treasury needs a note on PO vs DocuSign.
- Legal: Neha, can you take the force-majeure pricing carve-out and ensure it is narrowly scoped (GPU cost index threshold + mutual renegotiation language)? Also add the 30-day dispute window for true-ups.

I want to avoid large open-ended retroactive price exposure while keeping the MAP compelling. If you need to escalate for one-off credit approval, let me know and I'll route to revenue ops.

Thanks — planning to send the final redline back to Sara by EOD Friday.

—Lauren

From: Sara Patel <sara@cloudarc.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudarc.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & pilot economics — CloudArc pilot (evaluation -> commit milestones)

Lauren,

Thanks for the thorough responses and for narrowing the redline language. Procurement and legal reviewed the proposed edits and we can accept the terms with two small asks (both minor):

1) Keep the 12-month price protection, but add a notification period of 14 days before invoking the GPU-cost carve-out so we have time to review.
2) For audit sampling: include a clause that sampled audits will be run on a mutually agreed 72-hour window and Redwood will provide a single consolidated usage export for that window.

If that's acceptable we'll sign the SOW and route for DocuSign. I'll send the DocuSign request once you confirm.
